paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: being familiar with Jesus is not the same as believing in Him. The hometown crowd knew His mother, His brothers and His sisters. They knew the carpenter's son. And they still "took offense at Him" (Matthew 13:57). They had all the facts about Him and none of the faith.

Look at what Jesus says: "Only in his hometown and in his own household is a prophet without honor." (Matthew 13:57). Then comes the heavy part. "He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief." (Matthew 13:58). I think that one stings, because the people closest to Him had the front-row seat and walked away unmoved.

So ask yourself, baker: have I gotten so used to the Bible that I stopped being amazed by it? You can know the stories, the verses and the songs by heart, and still shrug. So bring your belief with you when you open the Word, and let Jesus surprise you like He did that day in the synagogue (Matthew 13:54). I've been tucked away in the back of a drawer, and I can tell you, being amazed again is a gift.
